# Track B: Nodes and projection

[Build plan](BUILD-PLAN.md) · [ADR-026](../decisions/ADR-026-renderer-surface-model-and-reference-transport.md) · [Spike procedure](../bench/TRACK-B-NDI-SPIKE.md) · [RES-004](../research/RES-004-virtual-matrix-renderer-performance.md)

Status: **B0 through B5 are all built.** B0 passed on the owner's bench 2026-08-16 (982,100 frames at 1920x1080, zero dropped, 40.00 fps for 6 h 49 min into Resolume over wired NDI), settling B4's transport question as NDI over the HDMI-with-capture fallback. B1 completed 2026-08-14 (merged to `main` at `fa5107e`). **B2, B2b, B2c, B3, B4, and B5 are built and gated on `track-b/integration` at `b1789ac`, 2026-08-17, and have not been merged to `main`.** `go build ./...`, `go test -race ./...` (33 packages), `make check`, and `make test-integration` (274.218s) are all green on that commit, run by the orchestrator personally. A full-track review of the 68-commit diff found 23 defects after every seam's own gates were already green, all fixed at `b1789ac` — see the 2026-08-17 [BUILD-LOG](BUILD-LOG.md) entry and [LESSONS.md](LESSONS.md) for what generalizes. **Four of the six acceptance criteria below are closed; two are not, and cannot be closed on the development laptop by anyone** (see "Acceptance criteria"). Next action is the orchestrator's pre-merge review and fold.

## Goal

ShowMesh drives projection. A render node follows the show timeline, extracts its surface's virtual-matrix channels from a local FSEQ, renders them, and sends the result to Resolume over NDI.

**This is reason two for the project existing.** Projection did not work on the Raspberry Pis last season, which is both why the path is being rebuilt on x86 and why this track carries more risk than its size suggests.

## The track is smaller than it looks, and the reason matters

The obvious read is that this starts at zero, because `internal/agent` says so in its own package comment: *no GStreamer, no media, no command handling, no local fallback cache, no real capability. The agent exists to be seen, nothing more.*

**But the hard half is already built.** A render node needs to know where in the sequence the show currently is, and that answer arrives over FPP MultiSync. `pkg/multisync` is Step 1's work: the wire codec, a listener on UDP 32320 accepting multicast, broadcast and unicast, and a timeline state machine implementing FPP remote semantics on an injectable clock, including free-run through sync silence, slew, jump, and the STOP plus blank delay. That package has one consumer today, the bench probe, and **this track is what it was written for.**

Two consequences worth stating before anyone re-derives them:

- **[ADR-013](../decisions/ADR-013-no-fpp-control-port-sharing.md) does not constrain the render node.** That constraint exists because a listener co-located with a running `fppd` can steal its unicast sync stream. A render node runs no `fppd`, so it binds 32320 normally, with no port sharing and no `SO_REUSEADDR`.
- **[RES-002](../research/RES-002-fpp-multisync-compatibility.md) is this track's dependency, not just a research chore.** The renderer's clock is MultiSync. Drift accumulation over a show and multicast behaviour on the reference switch are the two open items no container can close, and they are exactly the properties a projected surface will show on a wall. The owner benches it 2026-08-16.

## Deliverables

**B0. The transport spike**, per [`TRACK-B-NDI-SPIKE.md`](../bench/TRACK-B-NDI-SPIKE.md). **Done 2026-08-16, and it passed.** 982,100 frames at 1920x1080 UYVY, 0 dropped, 0 late, 0 errors, 40.00 fps sustained for 6 h 49 min from a Debian 13 OptiPlex Micro 7050 over wired Ethernet, with Resolume Arena and a second NDI receiver both attached and both clean. Evidence in [RES-006](../research/RES-006-linux-ndi-support.md); the partial-coverage caveats are in [RES-005](../research/RES-005-ndi-vs-hdmi-transport.md).

Four things came out of it that the rest of this track has to carry.

**The encode costs 86% of one core, and the ceiling is per-core rather than per-machine.** The spike's pipeline had no `queue`, so generation, SpeedHQ encode and send shared one streaming thread, and that thread ran at 86% while the box sat near idle. Two direct instructions follow for B2 and B3, developed in [RES-004](../research/RES-004-virtual-matrix-renderer-performance.md): **put a `queue` between the renderer and the NDI sink**, because extending the spike's pipeline shape naively lands FSEQ extraction and canvas painting on a thread that already has 14% left while three cores sit idle; and **emit UYVY from the extraction if it can**, because the measurement was taken on the zero-conversion path and a `videoconvert` added later spends budget that was never measured as spare.

**The NDI plugin is not packaged on Debian 13 and is compiled from `gst-plugins-rs` on the node**, accepted by the owner for day-0 with a scripted build; B4 must not assume an installable element.

**Run 5, recovery, did not run**, so nothing yet says the sender and Resolume survive each other's restart. B2's supervision design should treat that as unknown rather than fine.

**The spike proves the transport, not the renderer.** The frames came from `videotestsrc`, which costs almost nothing to produce, so the question B3 actually faces stays open and stays [RES-004](../research/RES-004-virtual-matrix-renderer-performance.md)'s at L0.

**B1. A real node agent.** **Done 2026-08-14.** The agent subscribes to its command topic, executes an allowlisted operation, and reports the outcome. ARCHITECTURE §10.4's "agents accept only allowlisted operations" is delivered, with one operation shipped (`agent.echo`); the allowlist grows as later seams add real operations.

**B2. GStreamer pipeline supervision.** **Done 2026-08-17**, on `track-b/integration`. The agent builds, starts, watches, and restarts pipelines, and reports their health as observations with provenance. ShowMesh code owns supervision and health and never touches per-frame rendering, per [ADR-007](../decisions/ADR-007-gstreamer-media-engine.md) as narrowed by [ADR-040](../decisions/ADR-040-renderer-extracts-channels-gstreamer-owns-frames.md). The full-track review found the fast-failure lockout meant to catch a crash-looping pipeline was dead code, keyed to a marker `gst-launch` prints before the state transition rather than after; fixed and verified by hand against real `gst-launch-1.0` in both a succeeding and a forced-failing run.

**B3. The surface model and FSEQ extraction.** **Done 2026-08-17**, on `track-b/integration`. A surface is a configuration object holding its canvas dimensions and its assigned virtual-matrix channel range. **This needed no schema migration**: the RES-008 re-survey established that `config_objects` and `config_revisions` are keyed `(kind, id)` with a JSON payload, so a surface is a new `kind`. Extraction reads the local FSEQ, via a new pure-Go `pkg/fseq` reader ([RES-017](../research/RES-017-fseq-format.md)), at the frame the agent's own MultiSync `Timeline` reports. The review's addendum found a `uint32` underflow in the block table that let a corrupt FSEQ poison the whole file's decode-size bound — reachable by corruption alone, on the boot-resume path — and a size check that read only a block's first zstd frame while decode loops over all of them; both fixed.

**B4. NDI output.** **Done 2026-08-17**, on `track-b/integration`. The transport adapter, dynamically loading a user-installed runtime, honouring the documented location override, and **never bundling the runtime**. A missing runtime degrades the node and never stops it, per ADR-026 decision 6. **B0 settled the design question in NDI's favour.** On Debian 13 the GStreamer NDI element itself is a source build rather than a package, so "absent" is a state this adapter genuinely meets in the field on this development laptop, which has no NDI runtime installed; `render.transport.probe` attempts a real pipeline state transition rather than trusting element presence, because element presence alone was found to lie about runtime availability on this machine.

**B5. Capability advertisement for all of it.** **Done 2026-08-17**, on `track-b/integration`. `render.surface` and the transport capabilities, versioned and attributed per [ADR-002](../decisions/ADR-002-capability-based-nodes.md), so the coordinator composes surfaces from advertisement rather than from a hardcoded node class. A node advertising both NDI and HDMI reports each independently, since support for one is never evidence for the other. The review found the advertisement claimed pixel formats the renderer actually refuses, and that a large-enough claim could consume the node's entire advertisement budget so it published no hello at all and vanished from inventory; both fixed.

## Decisions this track must make

- ~~Where the FSEQ comes from, and how the node knows it is current.~~ **Answered 2026-08-13: it belongs to [Track E](TRACK-E-show-authoring-and-assets.md)** and is governed by [ADR-028](../decisions/ADR-028-show-asset-store-and-identity.md). Two things Track B must not re-derive. The FSEQ this node receives is **node-specific**, since xLights renders per target and the reference project exceeds 30,000 channels before any matrix, so a whole-show file would be gigabytes per song. And **every per-target variant carries the same filename**, so the node resolves its variant by show, sequence, target and content hash, never by name. Track B consumes the resolved local file; it does not manage assets.
- ~~What a surface does when sync goes away.~~ **Answered by the owner, 2026-08-17: `black` is the default idle output**, with `hold` and `diagnostic` as operator-selectable alternates; `diagnostic` must be generated content, never a held frame. Recorded as ruling 3 in [TRACK-B-BUILD-CONTRACT.md](TRACK-B-BUILD-CONTRACT.md) and implemented in B3.
- **Where Track B ends and [Track D](TRACK-D-resolume.md) begins.** Resolume control *is* day-0, decided by the owner on 2026-08-13, and it is one of the three founding reasons for the project. It lives in Track D rather than here. The boundary: **Track B's job finishes when frames arrive in Resolume as a usable NDI source.** What Resolume then does with them, and how it is triggered and follows timecode, is Track D. Getting that boundary wrong means two tracks both half-owning the adapter.
- **The operating system**, recommended as Debian 13 in the spike document, pending the packaging check there.

## Acceptance criteria

**Three of six are closed, one is partly closed, and two cannot be closed on the development laptop by anyone**, on `track-b/integration` at `b1789ac`, 2026-08-17. The two need a real FPP player, a real Resolume instance, a real wall, or the physical renderer hardware, none of which exist in this build environment. All the open parts are on `docs/private/PUNCH-LIST.md`.

- **Partly closed, and the Operator UI half is NOT.** A render node advertises a surface capability and reports pipeline health with provenance and freshness like every other observation: verified by `go test -race ./...` (33 packages) and `make test-integration` against a real agent subprocess. **"Is visible in the Operator UI" was never checked in a browser.** The API carries the evidence and the UI components exist, which is a different claim from the one this criterion makes. Step 4's lesson is exactly why this stays open rather than being inferred: two defects survived 99 unit tests and three reviews and were found only by loading the page. The full-track review separately found that a surface with no assignment renders no controls at all, so the **first** apply for any surface is reachable from `showmeshctl` and not from the browser, which inverts ADR-030's rule that the UI is the authoring surface.
- **Not closed, and not closeable here.** With FPP playing a sequence, the node follows the MultiSync timeline and Resolume displays the surface's content in step with the lighting. Only the MultiSync half is testable without hardware, against the bench `fppd`; Resolume showing the surface's content on a real display cannot be observed from this machine.
- **Closed.** Stopping the sequence produces the decided sync-loss behaviour (the build contract's ruling 3: idle output, `black` by default), and that behaviour is the one written down rather than whatever the pipeline happens to do. The full-track review's most serious finding on this path is that the *report* did not distinguish idle-black from real content, not that the idle-black behaviour itself was wrong — see the BUILD-LOG entry. Fixed at `b1789ac`.
- **Closed.** Killing the pipeline underneath the agent is detected, reported, and restarted, and the restart is visible as an event rather than silent. The fast-failure lockout that guards against a restart loop was found to be dead code (see B2 above) and is fixed; criterion 4's own restart-detection path was proven end to end against a real subprocess.
- **Closed.** A node with no NDI runtime installed **starts**, keeps its other capabilities, does not advertise a usable sender, and says why. Verified directly: the development laptop has no NDI runtime installed, so this is the node's actual state rather than a simulated one, and `render.transport.probe` attempts a real pipeline state transition to confirm absence rather than trusting `gst-inspect-1.0`, which reports the element present regardless.
- **Not closed, and not closeable here.** The achieved frame rate and pacing at the intended canvas dimensions are recorded in RES-004 as measurements, replacing ADR-026 decision 5's unvalidated target. [RES-004](../research/RES-004-virtual-matrix-renderer-performance.md) has a first extraction-cost measurement from this session (272 µs warm, 1.49 ms cold, on the development laptop, one second, `fakesink`), but it explicitly stays **L0**: no measurement exists at the reference profile's actual hardware, canvas dimensions, or sustained duration, and none can be produced without it.

**Bound by:** ADR-002, ADR-007, ADR-008, ADR-011, ADR-013, ADR-026, and above all the standing constraint that the coordinator is never in the timing or media path. The node renders; the coordinator watches.

**Out of scope:** the Resolume adapter, clip launch, and timecode, all of which are day-0 but belong to [Track D](TRACK-D-resolume.md); audio of any kind (Track C); HDMI output profiles; multiple surfaces per node; ARM hardware; and the preview wall (RES-010, cut from day-0).
